tables.name: stations
tables.description: Docking stations where riders pick up and return bikes.

columns.name: station_id
columns.doc: Unique station identifier.

columns.name: station_name
columns.doc: Public name of the station.

columns.name: precinct
columns.doc: City precinct the station sits in.

columns.name: docks
columns.doc: Number of docking points installed at the station.

columns.name: status
columns.doc: Operating state code: 1 = under construction, 2 = open and in service, 3 = temporarily suspended, 4 = permanently closed.

columns.name: bike_id
columns.doc: Unique bike identifier.

columns.name: fleet_tag
columns.doc: Fleet number printed on the bike frame.

columns.name: kind
columns.doc: Bike category code: 1 = standard pedal bike, 2 = electric-assist bike, 3 = cargo bike.

columns.name: in_fleet_since
columns.doc: Date the bike joined the fleet, YYYY-MM-DD.

columns.name: odometer
columns.doc: Kilometres ridden since the bike's last depot service; reset to zero at every service.

columns.name: member_id
columns.doc: Unique member identifier.

columns.name: full_name
columns.doc: Member's full name.

columns.name: suburb
columns.doc: Suburb where the member lives.

columns.name: plan
columns.doc: Subscription code: 1 = pay-per-ride, 2 = monthly pass, 3 = annual pass, 4 = student concession.

columns.name: joined_on
columns.doc: Date the member signed up, YYYY-MM-DD.

tables.name: trips
tables.description: Completed rentals, one per ride from unlock to return.

columns.name: trip_id
columns.doc: Unique trip identifier.

columns.name: member_id
columns.doc: The member who took the trip.

columns.name: bike_id
columns.doc: The bike that was used.

columns.name: start_station_id
columns.doc: Station where the bike was unlocked.

columns.name: end_station_id
columns.doc: Station where the bike was returned.

columns.name: started_at
columns.doc: Moment the trip began, as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS in UTC; the city's local time is UTC-5.

columns.name: duration
columns.doc: Length of the ride in whole minutes.

columns.name: fare
columns.doc: Amount charged for the trip in ride credits; one credit is worth 50 cents.

tables.name: maintenance
tables.description: Repair jobs logged by the workshop.

columns.name: job_id
columns.doc: Unique repair job identifier.

columns.name: bike_id
columns.doc: The bike that was repaired.

columns.name: category
columns.doc: Repair type code: 1 = tire or puncture, 2 = brakes, 3 = battery or motor, 4 = chain or gears, 5 = frame or crash damage.

columns.name: reported_on
columns.doc: Date the fault was reported, YYYY-MM-DD.

columns.name: fixed_on
columns.doc: Date the repair was completed, YYYY-MM-DD.

columns.name: cost
columns.doc: Total cost of the job, labour and parts, in Canadian dollars.

questions.text: Which station can hold the most bikes?
questions.sql: SELECT station_name FROM stations ORDER BY docks DESC LIMIT 1

questions.text: Right now, how many stations are open for business?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM stations WHERE status = 2

needs_docs.fact: code 2 means the station is open and in service

questions.text: Tell me how many rides began before 8 in the morning.
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trips WHERE strftime('%H', started_at, '-5 hours') < '08'

needs_docs.fact: start times are stored in UTC and the city's local time is 5 hours behind (UTC-5)

questions.text: Give me the number of electric bikes in the fleet.
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bikes WHERE kind = 2

questions.text: In Canadian dollars, what is the total repair bill so far?

needs_docs.fact: job costs are recorded in Canadian dollars

questions.text: Altogether, how many dollars did riders pay in fares?

needs_docs.fact: fares are counted in ride credits and each credit is worth 50 cents, so dollars = credits x 0.5

questions.text: List the riders who hold an annual pass.
questions.sql: SELECT full_name FROM members WHERE plan = 3 ORDER BY full_name

questions.text: Show me the bikes that have covered more than 500 km since their last service.
questions.sql: SELECT fleet_tag FROM bikes WHERE odometer > 500 ORDER BY fleet_tag

needs_docs.fact: odometer is kilometres ridden since the last service and resets to zero at each service, not lifetime distance

questions.text: How many repair jobs were logged for brake problems?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM maintenance WHERE category = 2
SELECT full_name FROM members WHERE joined_on LIKE '2025%' ORDER BY full_name

readings.sql: SELECT s.station_name FROM stations s JOIN trips t ON t.start_station_id = s.station_id GROUP BY s.station_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT s.station_name FROM stations s JOIN trips t ON t.end_station_id = s.station_id GROUP BY s.station_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Station busyness is measured by how many trips depart from it.

readings.sql: SELECT m.full_name FROM members m JOIN trips t ON t.member_id = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT m.full_name FROM members m JOIN trips t ON t.member_id = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id ORDER BY SUM(t.fare) DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: When we call a member the best, we mean the rider with the largest number of trips.

ambiguous.text: How much did repairs cost us in January?

readings.sql: SELECT SUM(cost) FROM maintenance WHERE reported_on >= '2026-01-01' AND reported_on < '2026-02-01'
SELECT SUM(cost) FROM maintenance WHERE fixed_on >= '2026-01-01' AND fixed_on < '2026-02-01'

resolving_note.text: Repair spending is booked to the month in which the fault was first reported.

ambiguous.text: How long is a typical ride?

readings.sql: SELECT AVG(duration) FROM (SELECT duration FROM trips ORDER BY duration LIMIT 2 - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trips) % 2 OFFSET (SELECT (COUNT(*) - 1) / 2 FROM trips))

resolving_note.text: The usual way to describe a typical ride is the mean duration across all trips.

ambiguous.text: Which bike is in the worst shape?

readings.sql: SELECT b.fleet_tag FROM bikes b JOIN maintenance m ON m.bike_id = b.bike_id GROUP BY b.bike_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT fleet_tag FROM bikes ORDER BY odometer DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: A bike's condition is judged mainly by how many repair jobs it has needed.
